message.content:
Desserts come in a rainbow of hues—there isn’t a single “color of the dessert.”  
Here’s a quick snapshot of the most common shades you’ll see on a plate:

| Dessert | Typical Color(s) | Why it looks that way |
|---------|------------------|-----------------------|
| **Chocolate cake** | Dark brown, sometimes with a glossy chocolate glaze | Cocoa solids give the deep brown; a glaze adds shine. |
| **Vanilla ice cream** | Creamy white | Milk or cream base, no added color. |
| **Strawberry shortcake** | Pink to deep red | Fresh strawberries and sometimes a hint of pink frosting. |
| **Lemon meringue pie** | Yellow (lemon) + white (meringue) | Lemon curd gives the bright yellow; meringue is airy white. |
| **Fruit tart** | Multicolored (red, green, orange, purple) | Fresh fruit slices create a natural rainbow. |
| **Macarons** | Pastel pink, mint green, chocolate brown, etc. | Food dyes or natural ingredients (cocoa, matcha, beetroot). |
| **Pavlova** | White with a golden‑brown crust | Egg whites give the white interior; the outer shell caramelizes. |
| **Brownies** | Dark brown | Cocoa powder and chocolate chips. |
| **Cheesecake** | Creamy white | Cream cheese base; sometimes topped with fruit or chocolate. |

If you had a specific dessert in mind, let me know and I can tell you its typical color!
